To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extended constitutive relations are consistent with the continuum-scale mass balance equations and are applicable over the entire saturation range, including residual saturations.

the capillary pressure, the relative permeabilities, the interfacial area, and the saturation can be expressed as functions of a single variable, the nonwetting saturation, and that these constitutive relationships are valid in the range from residual saturation to the main drainage saturation.

(1) the relative permeability to the nonwetting phase is a monotonically increasing function of capillary pressure, (2) the interfacial area of the nonwetting fluid decreases monotonically with capillary pressure, and (3) the interfacially trapped nonwetting fluid saturations increase monotonically with decreasing capillary pressure.

the development and application of a pore network model to describe capillary pressures and interfacial area over the full range from residual wetting-phase saturation to residual nonwetting phase saturation.
the development of constitutive relationships for the range of residual nonwetting‐phase saturations.
constitutive relationships that describe the saturation, capillary‐pressure, relative permeabilities and interfacial-area dependence on fluid‐fluid configuration in porous media.

the extended constitutive relationship for capillary pressure, which is the most important of the extended relationships, is the same as the conventional constitutive relationship for the residual saturation, and the extended constitutive relation for the nonwetting-phase relative permeability is the same as that of the residual saturation.
